doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Mongo Santamaria and early recording sessions
title: The tune Mean Lean through its recordings
summary: Laws talks about his composition Mean Lean and its versions across several albums. He says it was first written on guitar.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: It’s here on Flute By-Laws that we see Mean Lean. As we talked off-mic, this is the first time I see it show up in your discography, but then it’s on In the Beginning, and then it reappears on Storm, then the Calm. So it seems to keep coming back into your repertoire. Do you want to talk about this particular composition?

Yeah, because so many people seem to show some interest in it, and it’s some nice jazz changes to play on. I remember we first recorded it on Flute By-Laws. Then I think we did another one with – let’s see. What’s the second one you say? I think – did I do it with Mongo? No, I did it – oh my God, I can’t remember.
You may have done it with Mongo, but I’m just looking at the ones under your name. It’s In the Beginning.
It’s in there, and then again, like I said, in Storm.

Okay, now, the one I did on In the Beginning is – I just heard it for the first time in many years, because somebody gave it – somebody sent it to me. I did it almost like a suite, because you had different rhythms, different attitudes toward the same theme. So that track lasted a long time, too. It must have been about 10 minutes to 15 minutes. Then, the last time, I did it because I was doing an all-Latin record with Joey Heredia on – no, that’s not the last time. I did it also on the Baila Cinderella record with Joey Heredia, and then I also did it with Storm, then the Calm, where I had my piano player, David Budway, do an arrangement on which I like a lot, as I’ve heard it more. So it was just a different attitude towards that thematic material. It made it fresh. It was suggested by these guys, to do it.
So you just knocked it out.
Yeah. You know what? I played that theme when I had learned to play the guitar. It was the first [Laws sings a few notes] – that was written on the guitar.
